The securities trade lifecycle involves all the business, operational and technological steps involved in a capital markets "trade" (buying or selling of a financial instrument), from the moment an "order" is received through the "execution" of the trade through its "settlement." 

In this course, you will learn everything you need to know from the World's leading securities operations expert, Mike Simmons.  Mike takes you behind the scenes to understand precisely how investment and banking operations work in settling securities.  At the end of the course, you will have a solid understanding of the detailed steps involved in a trade from the back office operations point of view. Some of the many things covered in this course include discussion of:


  1. Order initiation and delivery (Front office function)

  2. Risk management and order routing (middle office function)

  3. Order matching and conversion into trade (front office function)

  4. Affirmation and confirmation (back office function)

  5. Clearing and Settlement (back office function)

Who is Mike?  He has managed large-scale security operations for some of the major money center banks and had had decades of experience in exactly how securities and risk management operations work in practice.

courseDetails.title: Whistleblower Protection: Legal Frameworks & Ethics
courseDetails.shortDescription: A comprehensive guide to protected disclosures, corporate governance, ethical reporting, and legal risk management.
courseDetails.longDescription:
“This course contains the use of artificial intelligence.”

In the contemporary corporate landscape, the ability to identify, report, and manage internal misconduct is a critical component of operational resilience and regulatory compliance. Whistleblowing mechanisms serve as the primary defense against systemic fraud, safety violations, and reputational collapse. This course provides a rigorous, enterprise-grade examination of whistleblower protections, legal frameworks, and the managerial responsibilities necessary to maintain a compliant and ethical organization.


This curriculum is designed for professionals who require a deep understanding of the intersection between individual ethics, statutory law, and corporate governance. We move beyond basic definitions to explore the complex legal architectures established by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX), the Dodd-Frank Act, and OSHA regulations. Participants will gain the analytical skills to distinguish between personal grievances and legally protected disclosures, ensuring that organizational resources are focused on addressing genuine material risks.


The course is structured to guide learners through the entire lifecycle of a disclosure. It begins with the foundational principles of reportable misconduct, including financial fraud, harassment, and safety breaches. Following this, the curriculum details the specific statutory protections available to whistleblowers and the severe penalties associated with retaliation. A significant portion of the training is dedicated to the procedural mechanics of internal investigations, focusing on confidentiality, anonymity, and evidence preservation.


Furthermore, this course addresses the human element of compliance. It equips managers and leaders with strategies to foster "psychological safety," a cultural prerequisite that encourages early reporting and prevents issues from escalating into external scandals. By analyzing real-world case studies and investigation protocols, learners will understand how to operationalize transparency and accountability within their teams.


Key areas of focus include:

  • Legal & Regulatory Landscape: Comprehensive coverage of SOX, Dodd-Frank, and international directives affecting global organizations.

  • Operational Procedures: Best practices for utilizing hotlines, conducting intake, and managing the "discovery phase" of investigations.

  • Managerial Duty: Specific protocols for managers receiving reports, including immediate anti-retaliation steps and coordination with Legal/HR.

  • Risk Mitigation: Strategies to protect organizational reputation and financial stability through proactive internal controls.


This content is developed to meet the standards of corporate learning and development (L&D) departments, offering actionable insights for protecting both the whistleblower and the integrity of the institution.
targetAudiences: Compliance Officers, Risk Managers, and Internal Auditors seeking to update their regulatory knowledge.
Human Resources (HR) professionals responsible for employee relations and investigation protocols.
Corporate managers and team leaders required to handle employee concerns and ethical dilemmas.
Business students and professionals interested in corporate governance and business law.

courseDetails.title: Data Literacy for Product Owners
courseDetails.shortDescription: Understanding Data, Quality, and Limits
courseDetails.longDescription:
This course contains the use of artificial intelligence.

Duration: 21 Weeks · 105 Teaching Days
Audience: Non-technical Product Owners, AI PMs, Business Leaders
Data Literacy for Product Owners is a comprehensive, business-focused program designed to help product leaders understand how data, data quality, and AI readiness shape successful digital and AI-powered products.

This course is built for Product Owners, Product Managers, AI Product Managers, and business leaders who do not need to become data scientists, but do need to make confident decisions about data-driven products. You will learn how to evaluate whether data is useful, trustworthy, complete, biased, fresh, and ready to support product decisions or AI systems.

Across 21 weeks, learners explore how data is created, collected, structured, monitored, and used in real-world product environments. The course explains the difference between structured data, unstructured data, behavioral data, self-reported data, event data, logs, and third-party data sources. You will learn why data does not magically exist, how instrumentation shapes what teams can measure, and why poor data collection often leads to poor product outcomes.

A major focus of the course is data quality. Learners will examine key dimensions such as accuracy, completeness, consistency, freshness, data drift, and data decay. You will learn how small data quality issues can quietly create major business problems, especially when dashboards, metrics, and AI systems are trusted without proper validation.

The course also covers bias, representation, and data limits in a practical, non-technical way. You will understand concepts such as sampling bias, historical bias, proxy variables, missing users, majority vs minority data effects, and why data cannot always support strong fairness claims. These lessons help product leaders avoid overconfidence and make more responsible decisions.

For AI-focused products, this course explains why AI systems are probabilistic, why training data differs from live data, why labels and ground truth are difficult, and how issues like data leakage, concept drift, feedback loops, and silent degradation can break AI products after launch.

By the end of the course, learners will be able to assess data readiness, ask better questions of data teams, communicate data risk to stakeholders, evaluate feasibility, and make stronger go / no-go decisions for AI initiatives. The final capstone helps learners conduct a complete data readiness and risk review for an AI product.

This course is ideal for anyone who wants to lead AI and data-driven products with better judgment, clearer communication, and stronger cross-functional collaboration.

courseDetails.title: SoAI-Certified Professional: AI Infrastructure (NCP-AII)

courseDetails.longDescription:
The SoAI-Certified Professional: AI Infrastructure (NCP-AII) course is designed for advanced professionals who want to master GPU-powered infrastructure for large-scale AI workloads. As AI models grow in complexity, success depends not just on algorithms, but on the ability to design, optimize, and secure the AI infrastructure that powers them. This certification prepares you to build, manage, and scale cutting-edge environments that deliver performance, efficiency, and enterprise readiness.

You’ll begin with the foundations of AI infrastructure, exploring the critical role of GPUs, DPUs, and CPUs, and how they combine to accelerate machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) pipelines. From understanding CUDA programming, NGC (NVIDIA GPU Cloud) resources, and the Triton Inference Server, you’ll build a strong grounding in the NVIDIA ecosystem that underpins modern AI.

Next, the course dives into GPU resource management and virtualization, where you’ll gain hands-on experience with MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) configuration, GPU sharing and isolation, and virtual GPU (vGPU) setup. You’ll also learn how to integrate GPU workloads into Kubernetes clusters, ensuring efficient scheduling and scalability across multi-tenant environments.

The curriculum then addresses storage, networking, and data pipelines, covering high-speed interconnects like NVLink, Infiniband, and RDMA, as well as strategies for eliminating data movement bottlenecks. You’ll design end-to-end AI pipelines that handle ETL, training, and inference, ensuring seamless flow from raw data to production deployment.

Building on this, you’ll explore cluster orchestration and scalability, leveraging Kubernetes, Helm, Operators, and Kubeflow to orchestrate multi-GPU workloads. You’ll examine on-premises, cloud, and hybrid cluster topologies, enabling you to deploy flexible solutions tailored to enterprise needs.

Performance optimization is another core focus. You’ll learn how to profile GPU workloads using Nsight, DLProf, and nvtop, monitor GPU metrics, and apply TensorRT optimization to accelerate inference. The course emphasizes identifying bottlenecks, tuning systems, and ensuring workloads run at maximum efficiency.

Security and compliance are critical in enterprise AI. You’ll implement workload security policies, configure role-based access control (RBAC), and integrate DPUs with DOCA for advanced encryption and network isolation. You’ll also learn how to align infrastructure with GDPR, HIPAA, and FedRAMP standards, ensuring compliance for sensitive industries like healthcare and finance.

The course extends to edge AI infrastructure, with modules on NVIDIA Jetson and Orin devices, federated learning, and industrial IoT deployments. You’ll then master model deployment at scale using NGC and the Triton Inference Server, covering multi-framework serving, load balancing, and high-availability design.

Finally, real-world case studies and a capstone project let you design and present a full AI infrastructure architecture that meets enterprise requirements. Through labs, mock exams, and flashcards, you’ll be fully prepared for the NCP-AII certification exam.

By completing this program, you will gain the skills to architect, optimize, and secure enterprise-grade AI infrastructure that supports tomorrow’s most demanding workloads. This certification sets you apart as a leader in AI infrastructure engineering.

courseDetails.title: KI-Champion im Job: Workflows bauen, testen und messen
courseDetails.shortDescription: Lernen Sie, Anwendungsfälle zu finden, KI-Workflows zu bauen, ihre Zuverlässigkeit zu prüfen und ihre Wirkung zu messen.
courseDetails.longDescription:
Dieser Kurs wurde unter Zuhilfenahme von künstlicher Intelligenz erstellt.

Ein Kurs über die vollständige Methode: einen Prozess wählen, den Workflow bauen, testen, ob er zuverlässig ist, und messen, was sich verändert hat.

Viele Kurse zu KI am Arbeitsplatz hören beim Tool oder bei der Theorie auf. Dieser geht den ganzen Zyklus an einem echten Prozess aus Ihrer eigenen Arbeit durch und verwendet genauso viel Zeit auf Evaluierung und Messung wie auf das Bauen.

Was Sie im Kurs tun

Sie wählen einen Prozess. Sie beobachten ihn, bilden ihn ab und lernen zu messen, was er heute kostet, bevor Sie ein Tool anfassen. Sie klassifizieren die beteiligten Daten und gestalten den menschlichen Prüfpunkt. Sie bauen den Workflow, bringen ihn dann absichtlich zum Scheitern und lernen, ihn mit Struktur statt mit strengeren Formulierungen zu reparieren. Sie stellen ein Testset zusammen und bewerten seine Zuverlässigkeit. Sie üben, mit einer Kollegin oder einem Kollegen einen begrenzten Pilot durchzuführen. Sie lernen, den Ertrag ehrlich zu berechnen, einschließlich der menschlichen Prüfzeit, die viele Rechner weglassen. Und Sie üben, einen einseitigen Business Case zu entwerfen.

Der Abschnitt zur Evaluierung

In Abschnitt 6 geht es darum, wie man evaluiert: repräsentative Testsets, Kriterien für Korrektheit, Vergleich mit einer menschlichen Baseline und feindselige Inputs. Das ist der Unterschied zwischen „es hat funktioniert, als ich es ausprobiert habe“ und einer Evaluierung, die Sie vorzeigen können.

Ehrlich bei den Zahlen

Der Kurs begleitet die Halden Supply Group, einen fiktiven mittelgroßen Großhändler, durch den ganzen Bogen, und ihr berechneter Ertrag liegt unter der ursprünglichen Prognose. Das ist Absicht: So können Sie untersuchen, warum das passiert und wie man ein solches Ergebnis berichtet.

Enthaltene Materialien

  • 12 herunterladbare Vorlagen: Arbeitsbuch zur Chancen-Analyse, ROI-Rechner, Messblatt für den Ist-Zustand, Arbeitsblatt zur Datenklassifizierung, Risikobewertung, Workflow-Canvas, Spezifikation der Anweisungen, schriftliche Verfahrensanweisung, Evaluierungs-Kit, Pilotpaket, Adoptionspaket und ein 30-60-90-Tage-Fahrplan
  • 9 Arbeitsergebnisse, die Sie zu einem Business Case zusammenfügen können
  • 7 Quizze und 10 praktische Aufgaben, jede mit vollständig ausgearbeiteter Musterlösung
  • Eine Vorlage für einen 90-Tage-Plan

Keine Programmierung. Die Methoden hängen von keinem bestimmten Tool ab.

Die Ergebnisse hängen vom gewählten Prozess, Ihrem Umfeld und Ihrem Einsatz ab. Dieser Kurs vermittelt die Methode; er garantiert weder Einsparungen noch Renditezahlen noch bestimmte berufliche Ergebnisse.

courseDetails.title: Scrum dopo l'IA: cosa resta, cosa cambia, cosa scompare
courseDetails.shortDescription: Ripensate user story, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review e ruoli del team per lo sviluppo nativo IA.
courseDetails.longDescription:
In questo corso vengono utilizzati strumenti di intelligenza artificiale.

Se Claude, Copilot e gli agenti autonomi possono analizzare i requisiti, scrivere il codice, generare i test, revisionare le pull request e aggiornare la documentazione, quali parti di Scrum creano ancora valore e quali sono diventate, senza che ce ne accorgessimo, dei rituali?

La maggior parte dei corsi su IA e Agile insegna a svolgere le cerimonie di sempre un po' più in fretta. Questo corso pone la domanda più difficile: che cosa deve diventare Scrum quando produrre software non è più limitato dalla capacità di esecuzione umana?

Classificherete ogni pratica del vostro team in quattro categorie (Mantenere, Adattare, Eliminare e Aggiungere) con un test ripetibile, e ricostruirete lo Sprint intorno alla risposta

Che cosa rende diverso questo corso

  • Si basa su evidenze misurate, non su opinioni: DORA 2025, il sondaggio State of Code 2026 di Sonar, l'analisi di LinearB su 8,1 milioni di pull request e le ricerche sul campo dei custodi stessi del framework Scrum. Ogni dato è citato
  • Tratta ciò che quasi nessuno tratta: le pratiche da eliminare e i controlli di governance da aggiungere che Scrum non ha mai previsto
  • Corregge una convinzione diffusa nella maggior parte dei team Scrum. Cercate nella Guida Scrum "user story", "story point", "velocity" o "stima": non compare nessuno di questi termini. Lo verificherete voi stessi nella lezione tre
  • Circa una lezione su quattro è una dimostrazione reale, non una spiegazione: vedrete anche un risultato dell'IA plausibile, ben scritto e completamente sbagliato venire respinto in revisione. Le sessioni dimostrative si sono svolte in inglese; la narrazione italiana ne traduce i passaggi chiave

Costruirete otto artefatti pronti all'uso

  • Una valutazione Mantenere / Adattare / Eliminare / Aggiungere del vostro team
  • Un flusso di lavoro dello Sprint riprogettato
  • Una matrice delle responsabilità tra persone e IA
  • Una Definition of Done consapevole dell'IA
  • Un nuovo formato per il Daily Scrum
  • Una politica di escalation per gli agenti
  • Una checklist di governance
  • Un backlog nativo IA, scritto in formati da cui un agente può costruire

Tutto viene sviluppato insieme a un caso di studio continuo: un'azienda di software sanitario con 1.400 persone, a dodici mesi dall'introduzione degli agenti di programmazione, il cui output è triplicato mentre le cerimonie non sono cambiate affatto, e il cui responsabile della sicurezza clinica sta per porre una domanda a cui nessuno sa rispondere

A chi non è rivolto. Se cercate una raccolta di prompt per condurre uno stand-up migliore, questo non è il corso giusto. È pensato per chi ha l'autorità, o l'ambizione, di cambiare il modo in cui il proprio team lavora davvero

Her yapay zekâ sistemini Md. 6 ve Ek III'e göre sınıflandırmayı, Ek IV teknik dosyasını hazırlamayı, temel haklar etki değerlendirmesinin kapsamını belirleyip yürütmeyi ve yönetim kurulunuzun onaylayacağı 18 aylık bir yol haritası planlamayı öğreneceksiniz.

Gerçekçi tek bir Avrupa şirketi üzerine kurulu. Her kavram, her örnek ve her ödev, merkezi Berlin'de bulunan bir işe alım teknolojisi şirketi olan Lumora HR'da geçer. Lumora aynı anda yüksek riskli bir ön eleme sisteminin sağlayıcısı, şirket içi yapay zekâ araçlarının uygulayıcısı ve genel amaçlı bir yapay zekâ modeli üzerine ürün geliştiren bir alt kademe sağlayıcıdır. 7. ünitenin sonunda Lumora'yı bir müşterinin kanıt talebiyle başlayan krizden yönetim kuruluna sunulmaya hazır bir uyum yol haritasına taşımış olacaksınız. courseDetails.title: Éviter les échecs récurrents : méthode et routines
courseDetails.shortDescription: Revoir ses croyances, structurer ses routines et transformer les revers en actions concrètes
courseDetails.longDescription:
Il arrive de répéter les mêmes efforts sans comprendre pourquoi un projet n’avance pas, ou de perdre son élan après un revers. Ce cours propose une démarche de réflexion et d’action pour analyser ces situations plus clairement, ajuster ses habitudes et construire une progression plus régulière.


Le parcours commence par une méthode en plusieurs étapes pour examiner ce qui bloque, distinguer les faits de l’interprétation que l’on en fait et choisir une prochaine action réaliste. L’objectif n’est pas d’éviter toute difficulté ni de promettre un résultat automatique. Il s’agit de mieux comprendre ses décisions, de tirer des enseignements d’une tentative et de reprendre le travail avec un cadre plus précis.


Vous travaillerez ensuite sur des applications quotidiennes : préparer une routine simple, utiliser la régularité plutôt que l’intensité ponctuelle, revoir certaines croyances qui limitent l’action et interpréter un problème de manière plus utile. Les exemples servent de points de départ pour construire vos propres repères, selon votre situation personnelle ou professionnelle.


Dans ce cours, vous apprendrez à :


• analyser un revers sans le transformer en jugement définitif ;

• identifier les habitudes et interprétations qui freinent votre progression ;

• préparer une routine compatible avec votre quotidien ;

• transformer un objectif général en actions plus concrètes ;

• utiliser la régularité pour maintenir un effort dans le temps ;

• faire le point sur une tentative et choisir l’ajustement suivant.


Ce cours s’adresse aux personnes qui veulent structurer leur réflexion après un échec, améliorer leur manière d’avancer sur un projet ou retrouver une routine plus stable. Aucun prérequis n’est nécessaire. Un carnet ou un document de notes suffit pour réaliser les exercices et adapter les principes à votre propre contexte.


Ce cours présente des outils de développement personnel et des retours d’expérience. Il ne garantit pas la réussite d’un projet, un revenu, une transformation personnelle ni un résultat professionnel. Il ne remplace pas un accompagnement médical ou psychologique.

courseDetails.title: [FR] Cours de Certification Ingénieur Associé en IA

Faites passer vos compétences en IA au niveau supérieur avec le Cours de Certification d’Ingénieur Associé en IA — un programme pratique de niveau intermédiaire conçu pour vous aider à acquérir une expertise concrète en apprentissage automatique, deep learning et développement d’agents d’IA. Nous commençons par l’Ingénierie des Caractéristiques et l’Évaluation des Modèles, où vous apprendrez à préparer les données, à extraire des caractéristiques pertinentes et à évaluer la performance des modèles à l’aide de métriques comme la précision, le rappel, le F1 score et le ROC-AUC. Ces compétences sont essentielles pour créer des modèles fiables et prêts pour la production.

Ensuite, nous abordons les Algorithmes Avancés de Machine Learning, avec des implémentations concrètes des arbres de décision, forêts aléatoires, gradient boosting, XGBoost et apprentissage par ensemble. Vous apprendrez quand et comment utiliser chaque algorithme selon les types de données et les cas d’usage.

Nous plongeons ensuite dans les Fondamentaux des Réseaux Neuronaux et du Deep Learning, pour comprendre clairement les perceptrons, fonctions d’activation, rétropropagation et architectures de réseaux. Cette section pose les bases nécessaires pour créer vos propres modèles de deep learning.

Dans la section Algorithmes et Implémentations ML, vous programmerez différents algorithmes à partir de zéro. Vous consoliderez vos connaissances théoriques et pratiques tout en renforçant vos compétences en Python et en raisonnement mathématique.

Nous explorons ensuite le Machine Learning avec TensorFlow, où vous construirez, entraînerez et évaluerez des modèles avec l’un des frameworks de deep learning les plus utilisés. Vous apprendrez à créer des modèles Keras, manipuler les tenseurs et concevoir des boucles d’entraînement personnalisées, indispensables pour des solutions IA évolutives.

Puis, place à l’Apprentissage avec PyTorch, où vous découvrirez comment utiliser ce framework puissant et flexible pour implémenter des modèles allant de la régression logistique aux réseaux de neurones convolutifs (CNN). Vous comprendrez le fonctionnement d’autograd, les optimisateurs et la formation de modèles dans un environnement modulaire adapté à la recherche.

Enfin, nous introduisons Les Agents d’IA pour les Nuls, une section accessible mais puissante sur les agents autonomes et les architectures basées sur les agents. Vous découvrirez leur rôle dans la prise de décision, la planification et l’automatisation des tâches, avec des cas d’usage concrets comme les chatbots, les systèmes de recommandation et la coordination multi-agents.

À la fin du cours, vous serez capable de :

Rejoignez des milliers d’apprenants et obtenez dès aujourd’hui votre Certificat d’Ingénieur Associé en IA — votre prochaine étape vers une carrière complète en intelligence artificielle !

courseDetails.title: [FR] De la Recette au Chef : Devenez Ingénieur en LLM

courseDetails.longDescription:
Ce cours est traduit par l'IA de l'anglais vers le français afin que vous puissiez apprendre des technologies de pointe dans votre langue maternelle.

De la Recette au Chef : Devenez Ingénieur en LLM (avec des Analogies Culinaires) est un cours ludique et accessible aux débutants, qui vous apprend à maîtriser les Grands Modèles de Langage (LLMs) sans écrire une seule ligne de code. Que vous soyez curieux de l’intelligence artificielle, que vous souhaitiez entrer dans le monde des modèles de langage ou que vous visiez à devenir ingénieur en LLM, ce cours est votre porte d’entrée vers la compréhension et l’utilisation d’outils puissants comme ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini ou LLaMA. Nous simplifions les concepts techniques à l’aide de métaphores culinaires savoureuses—pour que vous passiez de cuisinier débutant à chef de l’IA en un rien de temps.

Vous explorerez comment les LLMs sont conçus, entraînés, déployés et évalués à travers des analogies faciles à comprendre. Imaginez la tokenisation comme la découpe de légumes, l’entraînement comme la cuisson en grande quantité, ou la création de prompts comme l’assaisonnement parfait d’un plat. Chaque module vous introduira à une nouvelle compétence : préparation des données, fine-tuning, évaluation et mise en production. À la fin du cours, vous comprendrez des concepts clés tels que l’architecture des modèles, le pré-entraînement, l’apprentissage par transfert, l’optimisation des prompts, les métriques d’évaluation comme la perplexité et le score BLEU, et vous saurez déployer vos propres applications alimentées par des LLMs à l’aide d’outils comme FastAPI, Gradio, Hugging Face Spaces et LangChain.

Ce cours s’adresse aux étudiants, enseignants, créateurs de contenu, entrepreneurs et professionnels issus de milieux non techniques qui souhaitent apprendre les bases de l’IA et développer des applications concrètes à l’aide de modèles de langage. Nous vous guiderons pas à pas tout au long du cycle de vie de l’IA—de « Qu’est-ce qu’un modèle de langage ? » à la création de votre propre chatbot, résumeur de texte ou moteur de recommandation. Vous apprendrez à utiliser des outils sans code, à expérimenter avec de vrais prompts, à ajuster des modèles existants, à évaluer les résultats, et même à explorer des carrières comme ingénieur en prompts, chef de produit IA ou architecte LLM.

Aucune expérience en programmation n’est requise. Vous apprendrez à communiquer avec les LLMs en langage naturel, à concevoir des prompts intelligents et efficaces, et à comprendre ce qui se passe en coulisses—de la collecte des données à la tokenisation, jusqu’au processus de prédiction du modèle et à ses besoins informatiques via GPU et TPU. Nous aborderons également la détection des biais, les hallucinations, les boucles de rétroaction et les stratégies pour surveiller et améliorer vos systèmes d’IA au fil du temps.

À la fin du cours, vous disposerez d’une base solide en théorie des LLMs, d’un portfolio de projets pratiques en IA, et de la confiance nécessaire pour entrer dans le monde en pleine expansion de l’IA générative. Que vous souhaitiez créer votre propre produit IA, rejoindre une startup, contribuer à des projets open source ou simplement impressionner vos amis avec vos connaissances en machine learning, ce cours vous y mènera—avec une assiette bien garnie de savoir et une touche de plaisir.

Si vous êtes prêt à passer de lecteur de recettes à chef en LLM, rejoignez-nous pour ce voyage gourmand au cœur des grands modèles de langage, où chaque concept est expliqué avec des analogies parlantes et des exemples concrets.

Course Overview

Welcome to ESG Community Engagement: Become a Force for Good — a practical course for professionals who want to build stronger relationships with communities and stakeholders while creating measurable social and business value.

Community engagement is a critical part of the Social dimension of ESG. But effective engagement goes beyond one-off initiatives or corporate communication. It requires understanding community needs, identifying and prioritizing stakeholders, building trust, developing structured engagement strategies, and measuring whether your initiatives actually make a difference.

In this course, you'll learn how to develop ESG community and stakeholder engagement strategies that align community needs with organizational objectives. You'll explore practical frameworks for stakeholder engagement, community collaboration, impact measurement, and long-term relationship building.

You'll also learn how to use AI and ChatGPT to analyze community feedback, support engagement planning, generate insights, and evaluate impact — while maintaining human judgment and responsible oversight.

Through real-world ESG case studies, practical tools, interactive AI Role Plays, and ready-to-use prompts, you'll learn how to turn community engagement from a well-intentioned activity into a structured, measurable ESG capability.

This course is designed for professionals asking:

  • “How do we align ESG commitments with real community and stakeholder needs?”

  • “How do we identify and prioritize the stakeholders that matter most?”

  • “How can we measure whether our community engagement initiatives actually create value?”

  • “How do we build trust and long-term relationships with communities and stakeholders?”

  • “How can AI and ChatGPT help us gather insights, plan engagement, and measure impact responsibly?”

  • “How do we move beyond performative ESG and create measurable social and business impact?”

If these questions reflect the challenges you face, this course provides practical frameworks, tools, and real-world examples to help you address them.

Why Stakeholder Engagement Matters

ESG is about more than reporting or meeting regulatory requirements. Organizations need to understand and engage the people and groups who influence—or are affected by—their decisions.

These stakeholders may include local communities, employees, customers, investors, suppliers, regulators, nonprofit organizations, community leaders, business partners, and other groups connected to the organization.

Effective stakeholder engagement helps organizations:

  • Identify and understand stakeholder needs, interests, and expectations

  • Build trust and stronger stakeholder relationships

  • Identify emerging social and reputational risks before they escalate

  • Improve decision-making through stakeholder feedback and community insights

  • Align ESG initiatives with community needs and business objectives

  • Develop stronger community partnerships and collaborative solutions

  • Create measurable, long-term value for communities, stakeholders, and the organization

Throughout this course, you'll learn how to identify and prioritize stakeholders, understand community needs, develop structured engagement strategies, build trusted relationships, and measure the impact of your community engagement initiatives.

  6. Use AI to Support Engagement — Apply ChatGPT and AI tools to analyze insights, plan activities, support decision-making, and improve engagement workflows.

  7. Connect Engagement to Business Strategy — Align community initiatives with ESG priorities and core business objectives to create sustainable social and business value.

  8. Learn from Real-World Applications — Analyze ESG community engagement case studies and apply key lessons through practical exercises and AI-powered Role Plays.

This progression helps you move from understanding ESG community and stakeholder engagement to designing, implementing, measuring, and improving engagement strategies in real-world organizational contexts.

Why Take This Course?

Effective community engagement is increasingly a strategic ESG capability. Organizations need professionals who can understand stakeholder expectations, build trusted relationships, translate community needs into action, and demonstrate meaningful impact.

This course will help you:

  • Turn ESG commitments into practical action by developing community and stakeholder engagement strategies that respond to real needs.

  • Connect community needs with business objectives to create initiatives that generate both social and organizational value.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What is ESG community engagement?

ESG community engagement is the process of building meaningful relationships between organizations and the communities affected by their activities. It involves understanding community needs, engaging relevant stakeholders, addressing social and environmental concerns, and developing initiatives that create measurable value for both communities and organizations.

Why is community engagement important in ESG?

Community engagement is an important part of the Social dimension of ESG. Effective engagement helps organizations understand community expectations, build trust, strengthen stakeholder relationships, identify emerging concerns, and develop initiatives that respond to real community needs while supporting long-term business objectives.

What is stakeholder engagement in ESG?

Stakeholder engagement is the structured process of identifying, understanding, and communicating with people or groups who can affect—or are affected by—an organization's decisions and activities. In ESG, effective stakeholder engagement helps organizations understand different interests and expectations, improve decision-making, manage risks, build trust, and align ESG initiatives with stakeholder needs.

What is stakeholder mapping and why is it important?

Stakeholder mapping is a method for identifying and prioritizing stakeholders based on factors such as their interests, influence, needs, and relationship to an organization or initiative. It helps organizations determine which stakeholders to engage, understand different perspectives, and select appropriate engagement and communication approaches.

What is the difference between stakeholder engagement and community engagement?

Stakeholder engagement is the broader concept. It can include employees, customers, investors, suppliers, regulators, business partners, nonprofit organizations, and communities.

Community engagement focuses specifically on building relationships with communities affected by or connected to an organization's activities.

Within ESG, the two often overlap: effective community engagement is an important part of a broader stakeholder engagement strategy.

How do I create an ESG community engagement strategy?

Start by understanding community needs and identifying key stakeholders. Then define clear objectives, prioritize stakeholder groups, select appropriate engagement methods, establish responsibilities and timelines, and define how success will be measured.

An effective strategy should connect community needs, stakeholder priorities, ESG objectives, and business goals, while allowing for continuous feedback and improvement.

How do I measure the impact of community engagement initiatives?

Community engagement impact can be measured using quantitative and qualitative indicators. These may include participation rates, stakeholder satisfaction, feedback and sentiment, trust levels, engagement quality, project outcomes, and longer-term social or environmental improvements.

How can AI and ChatGPT support community and stakeholder engagement?

AI tools such as ChatGPT can support engagement teams by helping analyze stakeholder feedback, identify patterns and emerging concerns, develop engagement plans, design surveys and workshops, generate communication ideas, and evaluate engagement outcomes.

The course includes practical ChatGPT prompts and examples while emphasizing that AI should support—not replace—human judgment, stakeholder dialogue, and responsible decision-making.

How can community and stakeholder engagement support business goals?

When aligned with organizational strategy, engagement can help strengthen stakeholder trust, identify risks and opportunities, improve decision-making, support ESG objectives, enhance reputation, and create stronger community partnerships.

The goal is to find areas where community interests, stakeholder expectations, and business objectives intersect, creating value for both the organization and the communities it serves.

courseDetails.title: Estadística: Ji-cuadrada y análisis de varianza con Excel
courseDetails.shortDescription: Hacer los cálculos fácilmente con Excel
courseDetails.longDescription:
Actualemente Excel es una de las programas más utilizadas en computación y su uso hace más sencillo el proceso de muchas operaciones matemáticas. Un par de poderosas herramientas para realizar pruebas estadísticas que se utilizan para encontrar relaciones entre variables son la prueba ji-cuadrada (o chi-cuadrada) y el análisis de varianza (ANOVA). La prueba de ji-cuadrada se utiliza para evaluar la relación entre variables categóricas, mientras que el ANOVA se usa para comparar medias entre más de dos grupos o colecciones.

Prueba de ji-cuadrada se utiliza para:

  • Determinar si los datos observados se ajustan a los valores esperados.

  • Evaluar la independencia o asociación entre variables categóricas.

  • Determinar si dos variables categóricas están relacionadas.

  • Probar una hipótesis en una investigación estadística.

El análisis de varianza (ANOVA) se utiliza para:

  • Determinar si hay diferencias significativas en las medias entre más de dos grupos.

  • Comparar medias de más de dos grupos

  • Se usa para determinar relaciones significativas entre medias más de 2 muestras

Ambas pruebas se utilizan para comparar la variación y distribución de diferentes grupos de datos

Los objetivos del curso son:

  • Introducir las distribuciones ji-cuadrada (o chi-cuadrada) y la distribución F. Aprender a usarlas en la inferencia estadística.

  • Utilizar la distribución ji-cuadrada para ver si las varianzas de los mismos datos son independientes entre sí.

  • Utilizar una prueba ji-cuadrada para probar si una muestra particular de datos está bien descrita por una distribución determinada.

  • Utilizar la distribución ji-cuadrada (o chi-cuadrada) para intervalos de confianza y prueba de hipótesis respecto a una sola varianza de población.

  • Comparar más de dos medias de población empleando el análisis de varianza o ANOVA.

  • Utilizar la distribución F en pruebas de hipótesis de dos varianzas de población.

El presente curso está enfocado a cualquier persona interesada en el análisis de varianza (ANOVA) y el uso de la ji-cuadrada (o chi-cuadrada) que manejen Excel que cuenten con conocimientos intermedios de Excel, una cuenta de Office 365 y conocimientos general en estadística. En todos los ejercicios contarás con los archivos correspondientes y los apuntes. También podrás poner a prueba tus conocimientos con los cuestionarios.
